name: Anti-Melanoma Differentiation-Associated Protein 5 Dermatomyositis
aliases: Clinically Amyopathic Dermatomyositis with Anti-MDA5 Antibodies

criteria.description: Presence of anti-MDA5 autoantibodies detected by immunoassay
Characteristic skin findings including Gottron papules, heliotrope rash, and palmar papules
Evidence of rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease on imaging and pulmonary function tests
Clinically amyopathic or mild muscle weakness with normal or mildly elevated muscle enzymes
Abnormal nailfold capillary changes consistent with dermatomyositis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anti-MDA5 antibodies plus characteristic cutaneous manifestations and evidence of interstitial lung disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Muscle involvement may be absent or mild, distinguishing it from classic dermatomyositis

pathognomonic.notes: Painful erythematous papules on the palmar surfaces
Violaceous papules over extensor surfaces of joints
Severe lung involvement leading to respiratory failure

common.notes: Often subtle or absent in many patients
Low-grade fever common during active disease

occasional.notes: Hyperkeratotic, fissured skin on lateral and palmar aspects of fingers
Difficulty swallowing due to oropharyngeal muscle involvement
Vasospasm of digits triggered by cold or stress
Unintentional weight loss during active disease

rare.notes: Calcium deposits in skin and subcutaneous tissues

laboratory: Presence of anti-MDA5 autoantibodies by ELISA or immunoprecipitation
Normal or mildly elevated creatine kinase
Elevated serum ferritin correlating with disease activity
imaging: High-resolution CT showing ground-glass opacities and consolidation consistent with interstitial lung disease
Nailfold capillaroscopy demonstrating capillary dropout and dilated loops
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; association with HLA-DRB1* alleles reported
other: Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive pattern and reduced diffusion capacity
Skin biopsy showing interface dermatitis with mucin deposition

distinguishingFeatures: Chronic rather than rapidly progressive ILD

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
Markedly elevated serum ferritin indicating high disease activity
references: Sato S, et al. Clinical features of anti-MDA5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2013.
Gono T, et al. Anti-MDA5 antibody and rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease in dermatomyositis. Autoimmun Rev. 2017.
Fujimoto M, et al. Clinical characteristics of anti-MDA5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis. J Dermatol. 2018.
